documents.title: Cardiology follow-up after STEMI
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group. Office visit 02/20/2024.
Re: William Howland, DOB 05/02/1952. NKDA.

Seen three months after his inferior STEMI treated with a mid-RCA drug-eluting stent (11/15/2023). No angina since discharge; back to walking and light yard work. No bleeding on warfarin plus clopidogrel.
Medications: warfarin per our anticoagulation clinic (currently 7.5 mg daily), clopidogrel 75 mg daily, metoprolol succinate 100 mg daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, insulin glargine 24 units nightly.
Exam: comfortable; prosthetic click crisp; lungs clear; no edema.
Plan: continue clopidogrel to complete 12 months (mid-November 2024), then warfarin alone. No other changes. Return in 6 months.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit and diabetes follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV plus chronic care, 73M.
Function: independent; still does his own yard; no falls; driving. Recall 3/3. PHQ-2 0. Proxy unchanged.
Cardiac: no chest pain or pressure since the 2023 stent. Occasional short flutters. Off clopidogrel since last November. Anticoag clinic INRs steady on 7.5 mg.
Diabetes: fasting 120s-140s. No lows. Eye exam July - no retinopathy. FIT negative in July.
Meds reviewed: warfarin 7.5 (clinic), metoprolol succinate 100, lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5, metformin 1000 BID, glargine 24 u, atorvastatin 40.
Exam: vitals as charted. Irregular rhythm, crisp valve click. Lungs clear. No edema. Feet: intact skin, monofilament normal, pulses palpable.
A/P: stable across the board. Annual labs drawn. Lung CT ordered for October. Flu shot - he'll get it at his pharmacy next month. Follow-up in about 3 months.

reports.text: ST-segment elevation in leads II, III and aVF. Right-sided precordial leads recorded: ST elevation in V4R.
reports.conclusion: Acute inferior ST-elevation myocardial infarction with right ventricular involvement.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department, 11/21/2025. Copy to primary care.

CC: chest pressure.
HPI: 73-year-old man with coronary disease and a myocardial infarction in 2023, mechanical aortic valve on warfarin, with central pressure-type chest pain into the left arm, breathlessness and sweating that began about 30 minutes before arrival while he was mulching leaves with his mower.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Vitals: BP 160/90, HR 98, RR 22.
Labs: troponin I 0.5 ng/mL (reference <0.04), creatinine 1.2, A1c 7.2%.
ECG: ST elevation II, III, aVF; right-sided leads with ST elevation in V4R.
Treatment: aspirin, nitroglycerin, morphine.
Course: cardiology consulted, recommended immediate PCI. Transfer to the catheterization lab was delayed about 15 minutes - the order had been taken as a repeat ECG; clarified on re-evaluation and the patient went to the lab.
Impression: inferior STEMI with right ventricular involvement.
Disposition: admitted to cardiology after PCI.

documents.title: Clopidogrel refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy requesting clopidogrel 75 mg daily - started at the hospital 11/25, 30-day supply. Not on our current med list. ED record from 11/21 is in the chart (inferior STEMI, stent); discharge summary not received yet. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: PCP response
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Approved, 90 days with 3 refills, so he doesn't run out over the holidays - cardiology's plan per the patient is a year. Requested the discharge summary. He is overdue for a visit; front desk to reach out.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary - inferior and RV STEMI
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Regional hospital, cardiology service. Admitted 11/21/2025 via the ED; discharged 11/25/2025.

Diagnosis: inferior ST-elevation myocardial infarction with right ventricular infarction.
Presentation: chest pressure to the left arm with breathlessness and sweating while doing yard work. BP 160/90, HR 98, RR 22. Troponin I 0.5 ng/mL. Creatinine 1.2. A1c 7.2%. ECG with inferior ST elevation and ST elevation in V4R.
Procedure: coronary angiography - proximal right coronary artery occlusion, treated with one drug-eluting stent.
Course: brief delay before transfer to the catheterization laboratory, as documented in the ED record. Otherwise uneventful.
Allergies: NKDA.
Discharge medications: clopidogrel 75 mg daily for 12 months (restarted); warfarin 7.5 mg daily per anticoagulation clinic; metoprolol succinate 100 mg daily; lisinopril 20 mg daily; amlodipine 5 mg daily; atorvastatin 40 mg daily; metformin 1000 mg twice daily; insulin glargine 24 units nightly.
Follow-up: cardiology in 6-8 weeks; primary care.

Outside cardiology group, visit 02/10/2026.
Re: William Howland, DOB 05/02/1952. Allergies: none known.

Follow-up after inferior STEMI with right ventricular involvement, proximal RCA stent 11/21/2025. No angina since discharge. No bleeding on warfarin and clopidogrel.
Exam: comfortable; crisp mechanical click; lungs clear; no edema.
Plan: clopidogrel through November 2026, then warfarin alone. Anticoagulation clinic continues. No other medication changes. Return in 6 months.
